note: Nonsteroidal MRAs (finerenone; esaxerenone and apararenone in Japan) went into diabetic kidney disease on hypertensive-rat kidney injury (uninephrectomised DOCA-salt, SHRSP, Dahl) rather than diabetic models; ARTS-DN, FIDELIO-DKD and ESAX-DN were the patient tests, with hyperkalaemia the on-target harm.
label: Diabetic kidney disease (nonsteroidal MRA)

engagement.model: Rat urinary Na+/K+ natriuresis under MR-agonist challenge
engagement.note: Rat natriuresis (urinary Na/K) was the PD read-out that set equinatriuretic finerenone:eplerenone doses; esaxerenone used the same assay in adrenalectomised rats (Arai 2015).
engagement.quote: Finerenone reduced cardiac hypertrophy, plasma prohormone of brain natriuretic peptide, and proteinuria more efficiently than eplerenone when comparing equinatriuretic doses.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; J Cardiovasc Pharmacol is paywalled. The rat numbers (natriuresis at 0.3 mg/kg, 3- to 10-fold eplerenone's potency) are in the FDA integrated review, which cites this paper.
engagement.judgement: Opened at Kolkhof 2014, the first paper to publish the natriuresis-matched design; Barfacker 2012 (ChemMedChem) describes the discovery but its abstract gives no rat PD, so it is not used as the opening.

engagement.model: Rat urinary Na+/K+ natriuresis under MR-agonist challenge
engagement.note: Healthy men under fludrocortisone (Study 13786, NCT01473108): finerenone was natriuretic at every dose 2.5-20 mg and 20 mg out-natriuresed 50 mg eplerenone, the ranking the rat gave.
engagement.short: Finerenone out-natriuresed eplerenone in healthy men
engagement.quote: 20 mg of finerenone in either the PEG solution or as 2 x 10-mg tablets was more effective in increasing natriuresis compared to eplerenone administered as a 50-mg dose.
engagement.confidence_note: Healthy volunteers, not DKD patients. Study 13786 was never published and NCT01473108 has no posted results (registered 2011-11-17, completed 2010-11); the FDA review is the only public record.
engagement.reason: Natriuresis ranking vs eplerenone held in men
engagement.judgement: The review holds both the rat result (0.3 mg/kg; 3-10x eplerenone) and Study 13786 but never sets them side by side, so the comparison is paired, not stated. A 20 mg vs 50 mg comparison gives direction, not a potency ratio. readout_tier is proximal: urinary Na/K under an exogenous MR-agonist challenge is the receptor's own transcriptional output, one step from occupancy.
engagement.magnitude_basis: finerenone-vs-eplerenone natriuretic potency ranking: rat 3-10x per mg/kg, human 20 mg > 50 mg; no ratio computable

dose.note: Rat regimen target: kidney and heart protection at natriuretic doses that do not lower blood pressure (minimum effective 1 mg/kg); no rat-to-human exposure bridge was published.
dose.quote: Finerenone treatment prevented deoxycorticosterone acetate-/salt-challenged rats from functional as well as structural heart and kidney damage at dosages not reducing systemic blood pressure.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. FDA review: renal parameters and pro-fibrotic gene expression 'all responded significantly at 1 mg/kg' in this model.
dose.judgement: The model's dose target is a PD one (natriuretic but sub-hypotensive), stated by the FDA review as 'dose levels that induced natriuresis in animals'; it is scored on that, not on a plasma exposure, because none was bridged.

dose.note: The rat's regimen target (natriuretic, non-hypotensive dosing) was reached at 2.5-20 mg in men; 20 mg sat under the rat 6-month NOAEL (6x/8x unbound) and FIDELIO-DKD met its primary at 10/20 mg.
dose.short: Natriuretic dose reached; margin and efficacy held
dose.quote: Finerenone showed natriuretic effects (log10(10xNa/K ratio)) at all doses that were tested (Table 110).
dose.confidence_note: The human dose was chosen from ARTS-DN UACR saturation ('largely saturated at 20 mg' in the review's exposure-response model), not from rat exposure; the rat-to-human link is the shared PD target, not a bridged AUC.
dose.reason: Natriuretic dose reached; efficacy and margin held
dose.judgement: Scored 'same' with margin_stated: the review's Table 22 gives rat 6-month NOAELs of 5 (M) / 1.5 (F) mg/kg, above the 1 mg/kg effective dose, at 308x/435x total (6x/8x unbound) the 20 mg clinical AUC, and patients were dosed to 20 mg without the toxicology findings (adrenal, electrolyte) beyond the on-target potassium rise scored in safety. v2 had this cell 'untested' for want of an exposure bridge; v3 asks whether the regimen target was reached and sufficed, which it was. Dog 9-month male NOAEL margin was only 3x (2x unbound), noted but not a stated block.
dose.magnitude_basis: no published rat-to-human exposure ratio; PD target (natriuresis) reached across the clinical dose range; rat NOAEL margin 6x/8x unbound at 20 mg

dose.model: Phase 2b population PK/exposure-response model (ARTS-DN, ARTS-DN Japan) simulating UACR, serum potassium and eGFR
dose.note: Phase 2b PK/PD model (ARTS-DN, ARTS-DN Japan): UACR effect saturates at 20 mg, potassium/eGFR effects attenuate; 10 and 20 mg picked for phase 3. Rule 6: dated to online publication (2019-10), not print (2020).
dose.quote: Our dose-exposure-response modeling and simulation indicates effects were largely saturated at finerenone 20 mg and doses of both 10 and 20 mg once daily appear safe and efficacious at reducing albuminuria.
dose.confidence_note: Open access (PMC7051931), abstract-level reading. Online 2019-10-04 (Crossref; PMID 31583611), print 2020-03. Built on patient phase 2b data, so it is an in-silico extrapolation to the phase 3 regimen, not a preclinical system.
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first publication of the dose-selection model; in scope as an in-silico model used to choose doses. The applicant's exposure-response analyses are in the Kerendia review, so model_filed true.

dose.model: Phase 2b population PK/exposure-response model (ARTS-DN, ARTS-DN Japan) simulating UACR, serum potassium and eGFR
dose.note: FDA set the phase 2b model's 20 mg saturation beside FIDELIO-DKD exposure-response: 10/20 mg gave sufficient exposure (EC50 0.165 vs 32 µg/L); primary met.
dose.short: Modelled 10/20 mg regimen sufficient in FIDELIO
dose.quote: In contrast, analyses of exposure-vs-time to the renal composite outcome suggest that the 10 mg and 20 mg doses provide sufficient exposure for the intended treatment effect.
dose.confidence_note: Verbatim from the integrated review's dose-regimen section, which also states 'Dose-exposure-response modeling and simulation indicate that effects of finerenone were largely saturated at 20 mg'. The tier-1 record of the same comparison is the FIDELIO-DKD dose-exposure-response paper (van den Berg, doi 10.1007/s40262-021-01082-2, epub 2021-11-13): 'Finerenone effects on kidney outcomes approached saturation towards 20 mg once daily'. The model's '10 and 20 mg appear safe' held with the titration scheme; the hyperkalaemia itself is scored on the safety tracks.
dose.judgement: Dose rule 'reached, drug worked': the modelled 10/20 mg regimen was the FIDELIO-DKD regimen, exposure sat far above the phase 3 EC50 and the primary was met. margin_stated true under decision 16: the model stated 10 and 20 mg were safe and efficacious and the trial dosed to that target without toxicity blocking it. Dated to the FDA review (2021), the earliest public statement of the comparison; the Clin Pharmacokinet paper came later the same year.
dose.reason: Modelled 10/20 mg regimen held in FIDELIO
dose.magnitude_basis: dose at which the effect saturates: model 20 mg; FIDELIO-DKD exposure-response 'approached saturation towards 20 mg once daily', EC50 0.166 µg/L against 32 µg/L steady state at 20 mg

efficacy.note: Uninephrectomised DOCA-salt rat: finerenone cut proteinuria, kidney and heart weight and pro-fibrotic genes versus equinatriuretic eplerenone; a hypertensive, not diabetic, kidney injury.
efficacy.short: DOCA-salt rat: less proteinuria and fibrosis
efficacy.quote: Finerenone treatment prevented deoxycorticosterone acetate-/salt-challenged rats from functional as well as structural heart and kidney damage at dosages not reducing systemic blood pressure.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The FDA review names this DOCA-salt/uninephrectomy rat plus SHRSP and post-MI rat as the filed primary pharmacology; no diabetic model is in the finerenone package (no db/db, STZ or Zucker study in the review).
efficacy.judgement: Esaxerenone's own DOCA-salt uninephrectomised rat (Arai 2016, 10.1124/jpet.116.234765) is the same system run for another drug, so it is its own esaxerenone track (entries 15-16); the Dahl salt-sensitive rat (Arai 2015) is a different system but carries the same proteinuria prediction and is folded into the safety cell instead, where its prediction differs.

efficacy.note: ARTS-DN primary (day-90 UACR ratio) met: placebo-corrected 0.62 at 20 mg, the clinical analogue of rat proteinuria, on top of ACEi/ARB; no steroidal comparator arm.
efficacy.quote: Finerenone demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction in UACR.
efficacy.judgement: Paired: the JAMA paper does not cite the rat. ARTS-DN was a phase 2b whose pre-specified primary was the UACR ratio, so endpoint_role is primary. outcome_tested is positive because FIDELIO-DKD later met a hard kidney composite; the status still follows the surrogate.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: proteinuria/UACR direction; the rat percentage proteinuria reduction is not on the same scale as a 0.62 placebo-corrected UACR ratio

patient_trials.quote: The primary outcome, the placebo-corrected mean ratio of the UACR at day 90 relative to baseline, was reduced in the finerenone 7.5-, 10-, 15-, and 20-mg/d groups

As a percentage of baseline, mean UACR decreased to 62.9%, 50.8%, and 46.5% in the 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg apararenone groups, respectively, at week 24 (placebo: 113.7% at week 24; all P < 0.001 vs placebo).

efficacy.note: FIDELIO-DKD primary (kidney failure, sustained >=40% eGFR fall, renal death) HR 0.82 for finerenone. Esaxerenone's ESAX-DN is scored on its own DOCA-salt track; apararenone was not dosed in this rat.
efficacy.short: Hard kidney outcomes met; three members positive
efficacy.quote: In patients with CKD and type 2 diabetes, treatment with finerenone resulted in lower risks of CKD progression and cardiovascular events than placebo.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for ESAX-DN and the apararenone phase 2; both are Japanese trials without ClinicalTrials.gov results postings (ESAX-DN is JAPIC-registered; apararenone NCT02517320 has no results posted).
efficacy.reason: Rat proteinuria drop held through to hard outcomes
efficacy.judgement: Strengthening entry, not a status change: a second and third member of the class, and an outcome trial, on the same track. Not 'neg': no nonsteroidal MRA has failed in DKD, and the rat gave no sub-bar signal for any member. Dated 2020 (NEJM epub 2020-10-23); registry results 2021-07-19.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: rat proteinuria versus a human hard-outcome hazard ratio; not on one scale

patient_trials.quote: a primary outcome event occurred in 504 of 2833 patients (17.8%) in the finerenone group and 600 of 2841 patients (21.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82
a primary outcome event occurred in 458 of 3686 patients (12.4%) in the finerenone group and in 519 of 3666 (14.2%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.87

Overall, 49 (22%) and nine (4%) patients in the esaxerenone and placebo groups, respectively, achieved urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio remission (absolute difference 18%; 95% confidence interval, 12% to 25%
The UACR-lowering effect of apararenone administered once daily for 24 weeks in patients with stage 2 DN was confirmed, and the 52-week administration was safe and tolerable.

efficacy.note: High-salt KK-Ay type-2-diabetic mouse, the first diabetic kidney model published for a member: esaxerenone 1 mg/kg cut albuminuria, glomerular injury and fibrosis more than spironolactone at equal blood pressure.
efficacy.short: Diabetic mouse: esaxerenone beats spironolactone on albuminuria
efficacy.quote: These data indicate for the first time that a nonsteroidal MR antagonist elicits renoprotective effects in DKD mice.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Academic (Kagawa) study, epub 2019-01-21: after the esaxerenone phase 2b in T2D microalbuminuria (NCT02345057, completed 2016-06) but before ESAX-DN read out, so it is not a retrodiction of the phase 3 primary.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from the DOCA-salt rat: a diabetic animal with a diabetes-specific prediction (albuminuria in a type 2 diabetic kidney), the only such system before ESAX-DN. Whether the model was filed with PMDA is unknown (esaxerenone is approved in Japan for hypertension only), so model_filed is null.

efficacy.note: Retrodiction: the KK-Ay mouse (2019-01) post-dates ARTS-DN's UACR answer for the target (2015); ESAX-DN's UACR remission 22% vs 4% matched its albuminuria drop.
efficacy.quote: Overall, 49 (22%) and nine (4%) patients in the esaxerenone and placebo groups, respectively, achieved urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio remission (absolute difference 18%; 95% confidence interval, 12% to 25%
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (CJASN full text not open on Europe PMC). The phase 2b (NCT02345057, published 2019) already showed dose-dependent UACR reduction before the mouse paper, so the class answer was partly known; scored against the phase 3 primary, which was not. No outcome trial exists for esaxerenone.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction rule for efficacy: a model result public after a patient result for the same target and action, from any drug, is a retrodiction; ARTS-DN (finerenone, 2015) showed the UACR fall before this mouse, so retro, not same. Paired with ESAX-DN, esaxerenone's own primary.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: albuminuria direction; mouse albumin excretion versus a remission-rate difference, not one scale

efficacy.model: Munich Wistar Frömter rat (spontaneous non-diabetic albuminuric CKD)
efficacy.note: Munich Wistar Frömter rat, a genetic non-diabetic albuminuric CKD model: finerenone 10 mg/kg for 4 weeks cut albuminuria >40% and lowered systolic blood pressure.
efficacy.quote: Finerenone lowered albuminuria by >40% and significantly reduced SBP in MWF.
efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC6189469); received 2018-06-14, published 2018-10-09. Not in the Kerendia integrated review (no Munich/Frömter/MWF hit), so model_filed false.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first use for a member. The paper itself post-dates ARTS-DN, so the track's scored entry is a retrodiction.

efficacy.model: Munich Wistar Frömter rat (spontaneous non-diabetic albuminuric CKD)
efficacy.note: The paper sets its >40% albuminuria drop beside ARTS-DN's dose-dependent UACR reduction (Bakris 2015), already public: a reproduction of the class answer, not a prediction.
efficacy.short: Non-diabetic CKD rat reproduces ARTS-DN albuminuria
efficacy.quote: In a recent study among patients with diabetic nephropathy receiving an ACEi or an ARB, the addition of finerenone compared with placebo resulted in improvement in the urinary albumin-creatinine ratio
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Model-side sentence in the same paper: 'Finerenone lead to a significant reduction (>40%) in albuminuria in the MWF model'. The paper also points to the then-pending FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD outcome trials (NCT02540993, NCT02545049), later positive. The comparison is the paper's own framing of its result against ARTS-DN, not a quantitative side-by-side.
efficacy.judgement: Decision 10 as adjudicated on the KK-Ay track: ARTS-DN (2015) had answered the class albuminuria question before this rat was run (received 2018-06) and the paper frames its result against that trial, so retro, not same; comparison stated by the source. Its own track rather than the DOCA-salt rat's: a different model (inherited nephron deficit, no mineralocorticoid excess) with a different prediction (albuminuria in non-diabetic CKD).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: albuminuria reduction: rat >40% at 10 mg/kg/day vs ARTS-DN placebo-corrected UACR reduction 35% at 20 mg (21-35% across 7.5-20 mg per the FDA review)

efficacy.model: Streptozotocin + high-fat/high-sucrose type 1 diabetic Munich Wistar Frömter rat
efficacy.note: New T1D DKD model (STZ 15 mg/kg + high-fat/high-sucrose in MWF rats): finerenone 10 mg/kg/day for 6 weeks suppressed Kim-1/Ngal, blood pressure and vascular damage.
efficacy.short: T1D MWF rat: finerenone suppresses kidney injury
efficacy.quote: D showed a 10-fold increase of kidney damage markers Kim-1 and Ngal which was significantly suppressed in D-FIN.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract plus scraped introduction (ScienceDirect); Europe PMC lists no PMC copy. Post-approval, so not in the Kerendia review.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. The model was built after FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD, so its only scored entry is a retrodiction.

efficacy.model: Streptozotocin + high-fat/high-sucrose type 1 diabetic Munich Wistar Frömter rat
efficacy.note: Model built after FIDELIO-DKD: the paper opens with finerenone's patient kidney and cardiovascular outcomes and reproduces kidney protection in a T1D rat.
efficacy.short: T1D rat reproduces FIDELIO kidney protection
efficacy.quote: The non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) finerenone (FIN) improves kidney and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) in type 2 diabetes (T2D).
efficacy.confidence_note: Scraped introduction also states: 'The recent results of two phase III trials, FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD ... provides robust evidence of both cardiovascular and kidney protection with FIN vs. placebo'. The model is type 1 diabetic while the patients were type 2, and its readouts (Kim-1/Ngal, blood pressure, pulse wave velocity) are not trial endpoints, so the reproduction is directional only.
efficacy.judgement: Decision 10: run after FIDELIO-DKD (2020) with the patient result stated as its premise, so retro. Its own track rather than the MWF rat's: diabetes induction makes a different model and the prediction (kidney injury markers, vascular damage) differs from the 2018 albuminuria prediction.
efficacy.reason: Post-FIDELIO T1D rat reproduces kidney protection
efficacy.magnitude_basis: rat kidney injury markers (Kim-1, Ngal) and vascular damage vs FIDELIO-DKD kidney composite HR 0.82; no common scale

efficacy.note: First verified member use of db/db mice: esaxerenone 1 mg/kg/day for 6 weeks suppressed renal macrophage proliferation; no albuminuria result in the abstract.
efficacy.short: db/db mouse: esaxerenone curbs macrophage proliferation
efficacy.quote: In vivo, esaxerenone treatment significantly suppressed macrophage proliferation.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract and scraped introduction only (paywalled). The introduction states esaxerenone's patient result ('Clinical trials have also shown that esaxerenone decreases the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio in patients with type 2 diabetes and microalbuminuria'), but the model readout is mechanistic, so it is not scored. An earlier member use of db/db may exist (the 2026 paper cites prior finerenone work in diabetic mice); not verified, so the opening year may be late.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry only. A stated patient result without a model readout that reproduces it is not a retrodiction match.

efficacy.note: Finerenone attenuated established kidney injury in db/db mice; the paper's premise is finerenone's renoprotection 'confirmed in DM and CKD patients', so it reproduces, not predicts.
efficacy.short: db/db mouse reproduces finerenone kidney protection
efficacy.quote: It was found in this research that the oral administration of finerenone attenuated the kidney injuries in established DN in db/db mice, and particularly improved the pathological changes in the renal tubulointerstitia.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Cells 2025, PMID 40072066, epub 2025-02-26, open access, UACR not read). Wang 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.bcp.2026.118370) repeats the result later: 'FIN treatment protected the kidneys against glomerular fibrosis in db/db mice', citing FIDELIO-DKD's 18% reduction.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction rule: the db/db finerenone run post-dates FIDELIO-DKD (2020) and states the patient benefit as its premise; kidney-injury protection reproduces the direction, so retro. Rule 6: Li 2025 is the earliest such comparison, so 2025, not Wang 2026. Finerenone's own track on db/db; esaxerenone's (Yang 2025) is separate.
efficacy.reason: Post-FIDELIO db/db mouse reproduces kidney protection
efficacy.magnitude_basis: kidney injury histology in db/db mice vs FIDELIO-DKD kidney composite HR 0.82; no common scale

efficacy.model: ZSF1 obese hypertensive type 2 diabetic rat
efficacy.note: ZSF1 rats, with raised UACR, BUN and renal fibrosis, given finerenone 10 mg/kg/day for 12 weeks: kidney function unchanged, renal hypertrophy reduced; the study is framed as an HFpEF model.
efficacy.short: ZSF1 rat: finerenone leaves kidney function unchanged
efficacy.quote: Finerenone treatment did not impact kidney function but reduced renal hypertrophy and cardiac fibrosis.
efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access full text read on mdpi.com (PMC9916671); first published 2023-01-28. Not in the Kerendia integrated review.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first use for a member drug; the paper post-dates FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD, so its scored entry is a retrodiction.

efficacy.model: ZSF1 obese hypertensive type 2 diabetic rat
efficacy.note: Run after FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD, which the paper cites, the ZSF1 rat failed to reproduce finerenone's albuminuria lowering: no change in UACR, BUN, glomerular or tubular injury, or renal fibrosis.
efficacy.short: Post-FIDELIO ZSF1 rat misses the UACR drop
efficacy.quote: The absence of albuminuria lowering effect of the MRA finerenone in ZSF1 rats may be intrinsic to the model (or to the treatment duration), but other studies are needed to clarify this point.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Results: 'The treatment of finerenone for 12 weeks had no impact on BUN ..., UACR ..., glomerular and tubular injuries ... or renal fibrosis'. The paper cites FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD as having shown renal benefit but does not set its UACR null against the patient UACR reduction itself.
efficacy.judgement: Decision 10: a retrodiction that failed to reproduce the known patient result (UACR -31% in FIDELIO-DKD, dose-dependent in ARTS-DN) is contra. Its own track: a different model (obese leptin-receptor-deficient T2D hypertensive rat) from the DOCA-salt, KK-Ay, MWF and db/db systems.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: no UACR change in ZSF1 rats at 10 mg/kg/day vs FIDELIO-DKD UACR -31% at 4 months
efficacy.reason: Post-FIDELIO ZSF1 rat fails to reproduce UACR drop

efficacy.note: Opening of the finerenone track on db/db mice: oral finerenone attenuated established diabetic kidney injury in db/db mice.
efficacy.short: db/db mouse: finerenone attenuates kidney injury
efficacy.quote: It was found in this research that the oral administration of finerenone attenuated the kidney injuries in established DN in db/db mice, and particularly improved the pathological changes in the renal tubulointerstitia.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for finerenone at the model's first verified use for that drug; appended at the end of the cell so existing indices hold.

efficacy.note: Esaxerenone (CS-3150) 0.3-3 mg/kg in the uninephrectomised DOCA-salt rat prevented and regressed proteinuria and renal injury.
efficacy.quote: Development of renal injury (proteinuria, renal hypertrophy, and histopathological changes in glomeruli and tubule) was also suppressed by CS-3150 with inhibition of mRNA expression of fibrosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress markers.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (JPET, PMID 27384074, epub 2016-07-06). Whether it was filed with PMDA is unknown.
efficacy.judgement: Opening of the esaxerenone track on the DOCA-salt rat, split from finerenone's; appended at the end of the cell.

efficacy.note: Retrodiction: esaxerenone's DOCA-salt rat (2016-07) post-dates ARTS-DN's UACR answer (2015); ESAX-DN's UACR-remission primary (22% vs 4%) matched its proteinuria drop.
efficacy.quote: Overall, 49 (22%) and nine (4%) patients in the esaxerenone and placebo groups, respectively, achieved urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio remission (absolute difference 18%; 95% confidence interval, 12% to 25%
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides (Arai 2016 JPET; Ito 2020 CJASN, epub 2020-11-25). ESAX-DN is JAPIC-registered with no CT.gov results record.
efficacy.judgement: Split from efficacy 3, which named ESAX-DN on the finerenone DOCA-salt track. Retrodiction rule for efficacy: the target's patient answer (ARTS-DN, 2015) was public before this rat, so retro, not same.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: rat proteinuria vs UACR remission-rate difference; not one scale

safety.note: Proxy opening at the IND. Chronic rat and dog toxicology showed exaggerated pharmacology: potassium and calcium up, sodium and chloride down, adrenal changes; it predicted a potassium rise.
safety.quote: The original IND was received on May 15, 2013.
safety.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy (IND receipt); the toxicology studies themselves are undated in the review and first became public with it in 2021.
safety.judgement: Separate track from the pharmacology rat: a different system (GLP toxicology, two species) with a different prediction (potassium will rise) from the tissue-distribution claim (less hyperkalaemia than steroidal MRAs).

safety.note: Toxicology's predicted potassium rise appeared: FIDELIO-DKD hyperkalaemia 18% vs 9%, discontinuation 2.3% vs 0.9%, hospitalisation 1.4% vs 0.3%, no fatal events; labelled as a Warning.
safety.quote: The most frequently reported adverse reaction was hyperkalemia, which was reported in 18% of patients randomized to finerenone as compared to 9% of patients randomized to placebo.
safety.confidence_note: Both sides are in the review (tox: 'mild impairment of electrolyte levels (increase in potassium and calcium, decrease in sodium and chloride)'); Agarwal 2022 (10.1681/ASN.2021070942) gives >=mild hyperkalaemia 21.4% vs 9.2%.
safety.judgement: The review ties the clinical risk to mechanism ('consistent with its mechanism of action'), not to the animal finding, so comparison_stated is false and the pairing is mine within one document. A matched prediction, so the harm is not double-counted with the dose cell, where the stated NOAEL margin held.
safety.magnitude_basis: direction of serum potassium; 'mild' electrolyte shift in animals versus a doubled hyperkalaemia adverse-event rate

safety.model: Rat whole-body autoradiography and equinatriuretic DOCA-salt comparison
safety.note: Whole-body autoradiography: finerenone distributes equally to rat heart and kidney (steroidal MRAs kidney-heavy); with equinatriuretic DOCA-salt data this was read as less hyperkalaemia per unit organ protection than steroidal MRAs.
safety.short: Balanced heart-kidney distribution predicts less hyperkalaemia
safety.quote: We conclude that finerenone may offer end-organ protection with a reduced risk of electrolyte disturbances.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The claim is relative to steroidal MRAs at equinatriuretic doses, not an absence of hyperkalaemia.
safety.judgement: Its own track: the prediction (less hyperkalaemia than steroidal MRAs) is different from toxicology's (potassium rises) and from the Dahl rat's (no hyperkalaemia).

safety.model: Rat whole-body autoradiography and equinatriuretic DOCA-salt comparison
safety.note: FDA's pharmacology reviewer set the Kolkhof/Naegele rat hypothesis beside the clinic and called the reduced-hyperkalaemia claim clinically supported; the only head-to-head is ARTS in HFrEF with CKD (5.3% vs 12.7% on spironolactone).
safety.short: Reviewer: less hyperkalaemia than steroidal, clinically supported
safety.quote: Clinical data available to date also support that the structural and pharmacological differences between finerenone and steroidal MRAs have clinical relevance in reducing adverse events such as hyperkalemia and sexual side-effects.
safety.confidence_note: A relative claim never tested head-to-head in DKD; finerenone still doubled hyperkalaemia versus placebo (18% vs 9%). The head-to-head is ARTS (Pitt 2013, Eur Heart J, 10.1093/eurheartj/eht187) in heart failure with mild-to-moderate CKD, a different indication; the reviewer's sentence is class-level, not a numeric rat-vs-trial potassium comparison.
safety.reason: Relative claim supported, untested head-to-head in DKD
safety.judgement: comparison_stated true: the review's EPC section quotes the preclinical equinatriuretic result (Kolkhof 2014), states the hyperkalaemia hypothesis it stimulated, then says clinical data support it. Scored 'same' at low confidence rather than 'contra' because the model promised less hyperkalaemia than steroidal MRAs, not none, and nothing in DKD contradicts that; imported_from is left null because the sentence is written in the DKD review, with the HF head-to-head only cited in support.
safety.magnitude_basis: hyperkalaemia rate relative to a steroidal MRA; no DKD head-to-head, so direction from ARTS (HF) only

safety.note: Dahl salt-sensitive rat on 8% salt: esaxerenone 0.25-2 mg/kg prevented hypertension, proteinuria and cardiorenal injury with no hyperkalaemia (>5.5 mEq/L), an absence claim at renoprotective doses.
safety.short: Dahl rat: renoprotection with no hyperkalaemia
safety.quote: The high salt diet significantly increased systolic blood pressure, which was prevented by treatment with CS-3150 in a dose-dependent manner with no hyperkalemia (>5.5mEq/L).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Rats were salt-loaded hypertensives without diabetes or RAS blockade. Whether this study was in the PMDA file is unknown (model_filed null).
safety.judgement: Its own track: a different system from the DOCA-salt rat and a different prediction (absence of hyperkalaemia, not merely less than steroidal). Its proteinuria prediction duplicates the DOCA-salt track and is not scored again in efficacy.

safety.note: Finerenone's FIDELIO-DKD set against the esaxerenone-dosed Dahl rat: hyperkalaemia 18% vs 9% (>=mild 21.4% vs 9.2%), discontinuations 2.3% vs 0.9%. Esaxerenone's own ESAX-DN result is entry 7.
safety.short: Rat 'no hyperkalaemia' failed in DKD patients
safety.quote: The incidence of hyperkalemia-related discontinuation of the trial regimen was higher with finerenone than with placebo (2.3% and 0.9%, respectively).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides. Patients were on maximal ACEi/ARB with eGFR 25-60 and the rat had neither, so part of the miss is population; but the species can show the harm (finerenone's 6-month rat toxicology did), so the absence claim is scored, not excused. Patient side is finerenone, not the drug dosed in the model.
safety.reason: Rat 'no hyperkalaemia' failed in DKD patients
safety.judgement: Scored 'contra' with magnitude 'opposite': the model stated no hyperkalaemia at renoprotective doses and the class doubled hyperkalaemia in DKD. An on-target harm is pooled across members, so finerenone's FIDELIO data test an esaxerenone-dosed rat (product_in_model false). ESAX-DN's own potassium numbers could not be quoted from the abstract, which is why the finerenone trial is the source.
safety.magnitude_basis: model: no hyperkalaemia >5.5 mEq/L at renoprotective doses; patients: hyperkalaemia adverse events doubled versus placebo

safety.note: Esaxerenone's own DKD patients: potassium >=5.5/6.0 mEq/L twice in 9% vs 2% on placebo in ESAX-DN, against the Dahl rat's 'no hyperkalaemia' at renoprotective doses.
safety.short: Dahl rat 'no hyperkalaemia' failed in ESAX-DN
safety.quote: More patients had a serum potassium level ≥6.0 or ≥5.5 mEq/L on two consecutive measurements in the esaxerenone group (20 [9%]) versus placebo (5 [2%])
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides (Ito 2020 CJASN, epub 2020-11-25). The esaxerenone phase 2b (Ito 2019, doi 10.2215/CJN.14751218) potassium data were not read and could date this earlier. Rats lacked CKD and RAS blockade.
safety.judgement: Split from safety 6: the rat was dosed with esaxerenone, so esaxerenone's own DKD trial is its product-matched track. contra, magnitude opposite: the model stated no hyperkalaemia and esaxerenone's DKD patients had more.
safety.magnitude_basis: model: no hyperkalaemia >5.5 mEq/L; patients: K >=5.5/6.0 twice 9% vs 2%
